doc_metadata.notes: Rated criteria response form for HR Advisory service category. Proponents must respond to six evaluation criteria: Corporate Profile, Key Personnel and Roster, Methodology & Advisory Approach, Thought Leadership & Innovation, Relationship Management, and Value-added services. Responses limited to 12 pages excluding resumes and work samples.
doc_metadata.title: APPENDIX D2 - RATED CRITERIA RESPONSE FORM – HR Advisory

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must describe their organisation, its purpose, structure and makeup, including profile and history, number of employees, products and services offered, range and depth of experience, core areas of expertise, and any requirements falling outside firm's scope.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to describe their organisation, its purpose, structure and makeup. Responses should include: Profile and history of the organisation; Number of employees; A list and description of the products and services you offer in support of the objectives and scope described in this service category, the range and depth of your experience with each, and identify which are your core areas of expertise or specialty; A list of any of our requirements that fall outside your firm's scope.
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.title: Corporate Profile

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must demonstrate capabilities and capacity by describing their team, including internal and external resources. Brief profiles (maximum half a page each) for maximum 4 individuals in dedicated relationship or coordination roles required, including name, proposed role, years of relevant experience, areas of specialization, professional designations, certifications, and credentials. Proponents must also describe practitioner talent available, range of expertise, vetting and development processes, quality and consistency standards, and typical resource assignment process.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to demonstrate their capabilities and capacity to provide the required services by describing their team, including internal and external resources. The response should include: A brief profile (no more than half a page) for each individual (maximum of 4) who would serve in a dedicated relationship or coordination role with the Bank — for example, an account manager, lead consultant, research specialist. These are the people we expect to interact with consistently, independent of any specific engagement. The profile should include: name and proposed role, years of relevant experience, areas of specialization, professional designations, certifications, and credentials. Describe the practitioner talent your firm can draw on, internally or externally. Rather than listing names or submitting bios for all potential resources, tell us about your bench/roster: the range of expertise available, how practitioners are vetted and developed, how you ensure quality and consistency when engaging associates or contractors, and what a typical resource assignment process looks like.
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.title: Key Personnel and Roster

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must describe their approach to delivering HR advisory services and managing consulting engagements, including methodology for assessing organizational needs and defining desired outcomes, approach to developing recommendations and implementation plans, governance model and project management approach, stakeholder engagement and consultation methodologies, change management and communication approaches where applicable, and quality assurance processes.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to describe their approach to delivering HR advisory services and managing consulting engagements. Responses should include: The methodology used to assess organizational needs and define desired outcomes; Approach to developing recommendations and implementation plans; Governance model and project management approach; Stakeholder engagement and consultation methodologies; Change management and communication approaches, where applicable; and Quality assurance processes.
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.title: Methodology & Advisory Approach

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must demonstrate ability to provide strategic insights, innovative solutions, and leading practices, including examples of innovative solutions or approaches implemented for clients, experience applying research, data analytics, benchmarking, or emerging HR practices to address client challenges, methods used to remain current with HR trends and industry developments, examples of recommendations that resulted in meaningful organizational improvements, and two (2) samples of published articles, white papers, research, frameworks, or thought leadership materials developed by the Proponent (maximum 2 pages per sample).

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to demonstrate their ability to provide strategic insights, innovative solutions, and leading practices for the requirements listed in section 4.1 of the RFP. Responses should include: Examples of innovative solutions or approaches implemented for clients; Experience applying research, data analytics, benchmarking, or emerging HR practices to address client challenges; Methods used to remain current with HR trends and industry developments; Examples of recommendations that resulted in meaningful organizational improvements; and Two (2) samples of published articles, white papers, research, frameworks, or thought leadership materials developed by the Proponent (maximum limit of 2 pages per sample).
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.title: Thought Leadership & Innovation

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must describe their approach to establishing, maintaining, and strengthening client relationships throughout the term of the Contract, including account management structure and governance processes, key client-facing roles and responsibilities, communication and reporting practices, approach to managing client expectations and competing priorities, escalation and issue-resolution procedures, methods used to monitor client satisfaction and obtain feedback, and an example of how the Proponent successfully responded to changing client requirements or resolved a significant client issue.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to describe their approach to establishing, maintaining, and strengthening client relationships throughout the term of the Contract. The response should include: Account management structure and governance processes; Key client-facing roles and responsibilities; Communication and reporting practices; Approach to managing client expectations and competing priorities; Escalation and issue-resolution procedures; Methods used to monitor client satisfaction and obtain feedback; and An example of how the Proponent successfully responded to changing client requirements or resolved a significant client issue.
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.title: Relationship Management

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must describe any additional, value-added services, tools, resources, or capabilities that would enhance the Bank's ability to achieve its HR objectives. For each value-added service, proponents must explain the benefit to the Bank, how it supports HR advisory objectives, and any conditions or limitations.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to describe any additional, value-added services, tools, resources, or capabilities that would enhance the Bank's ability to achieve its HR objectives.  For each value-added service, explain: The benefit to the Bank; How it supports HR advisory objectives; and Any conditions or limitations
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.title: Value-added

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must demonstrate experience providing strategic HR advisory services to organizations of similar size, complexity, and operating environment. Proponents must provide details for two (2) engagements completed within the last two (2) years, including client organization (or anonymized description if confidentiality applies), organizational size and sector, HR challenge or objective, scope of services provided, key deliverables, stakeholders involved, duration of the engagement, outcomes achieved and benefits realized, and client reference including contact name, title, email address, and telephone number.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to demonstrate experience providing strategic HR advisory services to organizations of similar size, complexity, and operating environment. Provide details for two (2) engagements completed within the last two (2) years, including: Client organization (or anonymized description if confidentiality applies); Organizational size and sector; HR challenge or objective; Scope of services provided; Key deliverables; Stakeholders involved; Duration of the engagement; Outcomes achieved and benefits realized; and Client reference, including contact name, title, email address, and telephone number.
source_refs.source_doc: Amendment1/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix D2 - Rated Criteria Response REVISED.docx

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must describe their organisation, its purpose, structure and makeup, including profile and history, number of employees, and list and description of off-the-shelf or custom products and services offered.

evaluation_criteria.title: Corporate Profile

evaluation_criteria.notes: Proponents must demonstrate capabilities and capacity by describing their team, including internal and external resources. Maximum 4 key personnel profiles (half page each) required for dedicated relationship/coordination roles. Bench/roster description required showing range of expertise, vetting and development processes, quality assurance, and resource assignment process.

source_refs.excerpt: Proponents are to demonstrate their capabilities and capacity to provide the required services by describing their team, including internal and external resources. The response should include: A brief profile (no more than half a page) for each individual (maximum of 4) who would serve in a dedicated relationship or coordination role with the Bank — for example, an account manager, instructional designer or project manager.

evaluation_criteria.notes: Review up to 20 Bank documents, workforce datasets, conduct 15 stakeholder interviews (60 minutes each), one 3-hour validation session, assess workforce planning practices, and develop workforce planning assessment.

source_refs.excerpt: Specs - Discovery and assessment: Assume: Review up to twenty (20) Bank documents, including workforce data, HR reports, planning documents, and organizational information; Review workforce datasets, including demographics, movement trends, vacancies, retirement eligibility, workforce planning metrics, and related indicators; Conduct fifteen (15) stakeholder interviews of sixty (60) minutes each with HR and senior business leaders on workforce priorities, risks, succession, talent needs, and future capabilities; Conduct one (1) three-hour stakeholder validation session to review findings, validate observations, and discuss priority workforce planning considerations; Assess current workforce planning practices, workforce risks, and workforce-related challenges; Identify current and future workforce capability requirements; and Develop a workforce planning assessment summarizing key findings, risks, opportunities, and observations.
source_refs.source_doc: OriginalRevision/RFP 2026-026 - Appendix E - Pricing Form.xlsx

commercial_clauses.source_fact: Service Provider acknowledges that all information received from Bank in connection with provision of Services and all information developed as part of Services is confidential, including identity of parties and fact of contact. Information is not confidential if: (i) generally available to public or becomes so through no fault of Service Provider; (ii) already known to, in possession of, or developed by Service Provider as documented by written records prior to Bank disclosure; or (iii) received in good faith on non-confidential basis from third party who lawfully obtained and disclosed it.

source_refs.excerpt: The Service Provider acknowledges that all information which it receives from the Bank in the course or in connection with the provision of the Services and all information which the Service Provider develops as part of the Services is to be considered as confidential in nature for the purposes of this Agreement including the identity of the parties and the fact that the parties are in contact with each other (collectively "Confidential Information"). However, information is not to be considered as "Confidential Information" if it is: generally available to the public or becomes so available through no fault of the Service Provider; already known to, in the possession of, or developed by the Service Provider, as documented by reasonably convincing written records possessed by the Service Provider prior to the disclosure by the Bank; or received by the Service Provider in good faith and on a non-confidential basis from a third party who lawfully obtained and disclosed such information to the Service Provider.

commercial_clauses.source_fact: In the event of an actual or suspected Data Breach, the Service Provider shall notify the Bank in writing without undue delay, and in any case, no later than forty-eight (48) hours after becoming aware of the breach. Data Breach is defined as any incident, whether actual or suspected, in which Bank data or Personal Information is accessed, used, or disclosed without authorization; lost, stolen, or destroyed without authorization; altered or modified without proper authorization including due to system vulnerability or human error; or subjected to any other event that may result in unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of Bank data or Personal Information. Notification shall be made to pace-cepa@bank-banque-canada.ca and shall include all known details of the breach at the time of discovery and updates as additional information becomes available.

source_refs.excerpt: In the event of an actual or suspected Data Breach, the Service Provider shall notify the Bank in writing without undue delay, and in any case, no later than forty-eight (48) hours after becoming aware of the breach. "Data Breach" means any incident, whether actual or suspected, in which Bank data or Personal Information is: Accessed, used, or disclosed without authorization; Lost, stolen, or destroyed without authorization; Altered or modified without proper authorization, including due to a system vulnerability or human error; or Subjected to any other event or series of events that may result in the unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of Bank data or Personal Information, including exposure or compromise in a manner that could reasonably be expected to cause harm to Bank or to any individual whose Personal Information has been affected. Notification shall be made to: pace-cepa@bank-banque-canada.ca. The notification shall include all known details of the breach at the time of discovery and updates as additional information becomes available.

evaluation_criteria.notes: The Bank will review proposals to determine whether mandatory criteria as set out in section 4.4 RFP Particulars – Mandatory criteria have been met. Failure to meet any mandatory criterion results in proposal disqualification.

source_refs.source_doc: RFP 2026-026 - Talent, Learning and Organizational Development Services.pdf

evaluation_criteria.title: Mandatory criteria

evaluation_criteria.notes: The Bank will review proposals to determine whether minimum qualification requirements as set out in Appendix C1 / C2 / C3 (as applicable) have been met. Failure to meet minimum qualification requirements results in proposal disqualification.

source_refs.excerpt: b. Minimum qualification requirements. evaluation_criteria.title: Minimum qualification requirements

evaluation_criteria.notes: If compliant with applicable mandatory criteria and minimum qualification requirements, the Bank will evaluate each qualified proposal based on non-price rated criteria as set out in section 4.5 RFP Particulars – Rated criteria and Appendix D1/D2/D3 (as applicable).

source_refs.excerpt: c. Rated criteria. If compliant with the applicable mandatory criteria and minimum qualification requirements, the Bank will evaluate each qualified proposal based on the non-price rated criteria as set out in section 4.5 RFP Particulars – Rated criteria and Appendix D1/D2/D3 (as applicable).
source_refs.source_doc: RFP 2026-026 - Talent, Learning and Organizational Development Services.pdf

evaluation_criteria.title: Rated criteria

evaluation_criteria.notes: Up to seven (7) top-ranked proponents for service category 1 and up to nine (9) top-ranked proponents for service category 3 may be invited to presentations with the Evaluation Committee. Presentations will validate proponents' ability to deliver required services and will be assessed on a pass/fail basis. Presentations will not be required for service category 2. Proponents may not disclose pricing information at this stage.

source_refs.excerpt: Stage 3. Presentation/Demonstration (virtual). As part of the evaluation process, up to seven (7) top-ranked proponents for service category 1; and up to nine (9) top-ranked proponents for service category 3 May be invited to presentations with the Evaluation Committee. These presentations will validate proponents' ability to deliver the required services and will be assessed on a pass/fail basis. Proponents may not disclose pricing information at this stage. Presentations will not be required for service category 2.
source_refs.source_doc: RFP 2026-026 - Talent, Learning and Organizational Development Services.pdf

evaluation_criteria.title: Stage 3. Presentation/Demonstration (virtual)

evaluation_criteria.notes: Review and scoring of submitted pricing of each qualified proposal in accordance with the price evaluation method set out in section 4.6 RFP Particulars – Price evaluation method. Price evaluation will be undertaken after evaluation of mandatory requirements and non-price rated criteria has been completed. If pricing appears abnormally low, the Bank may require detailed explanation.

source_refs.excerpt: Stage 4. Pricing. Stage 4 will consist of a review and scoring of the submitted pricing of each qualified proposal in accordance with the price evaluation method set out in section 4.6 RFP Particulars – Price evaluation method. The evaluation of price will be undertaken after the evaluation of mandatory requirements and non-price rated criteria has been completed.
source_refs.source_doc: RFP 2026-026 - Talent, Learning and Organizational Development Services.pdf

evaluation_criteria.title: Stage 4. Pricing

evaluation_criteria.notes: Scores from Stage 2, Stage 3 and Stage 4 are totalled. Highest-scoring proponents within each service category invited to negotiate. In event of tie, highest score on rated criteria determines selection. Awards made on category-by-category basis.

source_refs.excerpt: At Stage 5, the scores from Stage 2, Stage 3 and Stage 4 will be totalled and, subject to the terms of this RFP, the highest-scoring proponents within each service category will be invited to negotiate agreements based on the Form of Agreement in Appendix F, if reference checks are successful. In the event of a tie between proponents, the selected proponent will be decided by way of the highest score on the rated criteria.
